commit.message: test(desktop): cover rendered Magi SDK interactions

specification.objective: MAGI-012: run real React DOM user-interaction tests for Magi Desktop via the Hermes SDK style, with mocked SDK and ctx.rest and no services, credentials or real user profile.

requirements.statement: Render the unchanged Magi Desktop plugin with a minimal Vitest, React Testing Library and jsdom harness aligned with Hermes Desktop test tooling; no browser or external network used at test runtime.

Assert real user interactions across pending selection/search/refresh/errors, approval/rejection and bulk confirmation, stored editing with stale/error behavior, keyboard controls, compaction preview/cancel/apply; describe absent advanced features as limitations.
Ensure deterministic mocks and CI execution on an explicit Node version, provide reproducible commands and document interactions actually verified.

acceptance_criteria.statement: New test verifies interaction runner exists and executes live render/user actions, which fails on baseline where harness is absent.

Harness tests selection, filter, REST failures and retries, pending decision confirmation, stored edit/add/delete, and compaction preview/cancel/apply, with meaningful expectations on DOM and outbound mocked REST.
npm CI lock, local command, verify.sh and CI integration execute deterministically; tests do not contact network or user Hermes stores, and changelog states known gaps.

invariants.statement: No edits to Hermes, Magi production UI or Python backend; existing 013/020 quality behaviors and version 1.7.8 preserved.

forbidden_states.statement: Test interacts with real Hermes credentials, profile, memory files, or external endpoints.

inputs.statement: Baseline d6f8cf3 and Hermes Desktop official Vitest + React Testing Library + jsdom conventions.

outputs.statement: React DOM interaction tests, deterministic SDK/REST harness and script, CI setup and README/changelog.

failure_semantics.statement: Failed DOM expectation or REST call leads to nonzero test script exit and CI failure; unsupported functionality is documented rather than falsely certified.
